newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek govt will not back down with farmers.
newsitem.headline: Greek govt will not back down with farmers.

text.p: Greece's socialist government will stick to its economic policies and will not bow to blackmail by thousands of farmers blockading national road and rail links, National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou said on Monday.
"The government cannot and will not surrender to blackmail. It is obliged, like every democratic government, to secure the working of the economy and the state," he told reporters at his ministry.

He said Greece's socialist government, elected on a fresh four-year mandate in September, would not be sidetracked from implementing its economic programme. "It is inconceivable that a social group seeks to impose its will on an entire society," Papandoniou said.
Farmers have paralyzed the nation's road and rail network for 12 days, blocking nearly 100 points around the country to press their list of economic demands.
Papandoniou said the government, after several attempts at negotiations, had done all it could to solve farmers' problems within the framework of the 1997 budget and Greece's economic situation.

Referring to the sharp fall in November inflation, down to 7.7 percent year-on-year from 8.3 percent in October, he said the economy was on the right track and expected another drop in inflation in December.
